Deeply nested replies beyond 3 levels are collapsed with expandable 'Show more replies' controls. Comments ordered chronologically (oldest first by default, with sort options available). This array includes only active comments with status='published'. Deleted comments and moderated comments are excluded from this array.

attachments.description: All file and image attachments associated with this article. Images (JPEG, PNG, GIF, WebP) are optimized and displayed inline within article content at responsive widths (600px maximum on desktop, scaled for mobile devices). Documents (PDF, DOCX, TXT, ZIP, and other supported formats) are presented as downloadable files with filename, file size in human-readable format, and file type icon. Attachments are stored in discussion_board_attachments table with polymorphic reference (attachable_type='article', discussion_board_article_id matching this article's id). Maximum 10 attachments per article, 100 MB total combined size limit enforced. Only includes attachments with security_status='safe' (passed antivirus/malware scanning). Deleted attachments (deleted_at is not NULL) are excluded from this array.

IDiscussionBoardArticle.description:
Complete article entity with all metadata, content, engagement metrics, and associated comments and attachments. Returned after article creation, updates, or moderation actions. Includes article identification, authorship information, content body with markdown formatting support, category assignment, view count tracking, modification history through revision number, and moderation status. Comments are included as nested array showing threaded discussions. Attachments are included showing all images displayed inline and files available for download. Articles serve as the primary discussion units in the platform where members initiate discussions on economic and political topics.

The article status field indicates visibility: 'published' articles are visible to all users, 'archived' articles are hidden from regular users by moderators. Moderation actions update this status and create audit log entries. View count tracks engagement and is incremented on each unique view within a 24-hour deduplication window. Revision number tracks how many times article has been edited. Timestamps support audit trail and content history tracking.

title.description: Updated article title between 3 and 200 characters. Optional field allowing author or moderator to modify the article's title after creation. Must contain meaningful text (letters or numbers). If provided, replaces the current title in the article.

content.description: Updated article body text between 10 and 50,000 characters. Optional field allowing author or moderator to modify the substantive discussion content. Supports basic markdown formatting. If provided, replaces the current article content and creates a new revision record for audit trail.

category.description: Updated category ID for the article. References discussion_board_categories.id. Optional field that allows article category to be changed. Valid categories are Economics and Politics. If provided, updates the article's category assignment. Note: Some implementations may make this immutable after creation per business rules.

attachments_to_add.description: Optional array of new file and image attachments to add to the article during update. Each attachment is validated for supported file type (images: JPEG, PNG, GIF, WebP; documents: PDF, DOCX, XLSX, TXT, ZIP, RAR, 7Z, and others), file size limits (images 10 MB max, documents 20 MB max, archives 50 MB max per file), and security status (malware scanning). System enforces total article constraints: maximum 10 total attachments (existing + new combined), 100 MB total combined size. If adding new attachments would exceed these limits, the operation is rejected with specific error message. Attachments are processed and stored before article update is completed. If any attachment fails validation, the entire update operation is aborted and article remains unchanged. Empty array or omitted means no attachments are being added.

attachments_to_remove.description: Optional array of attachment IDs to remove from the article during update. Each specified attachment ID must reference an existing attachment (discussion_board_attachments.id) currently associated with this article. When an attachment is removed, the file is deleted from storage and the attachment record is removed or soft-deleted from the database. Members can only remove attachments they uploaded; moderators can remove any attachment. If any specified attachment ID does not exist or does not belong to this article, that removal is rejected with specific error message. Empty array or omitted means no attachments are being removed.

IDiscussionBoardArticle.IUpdate.description:
Update request body for modifying an existing article including title, content, category assignment, and attachment management. All fields are optional, allowing partial updates. Only the fields provided will be updated in the article record. The system preserves fields that are not included in the update request.

When an article is updated, the system creates a new revision record in discussion_board_article_revisions table preserving the previous version for complete audit trail. The revision_number is incremented to track the edit count. The updated_at timestamp is set to the current time to reflect the modification, while the original created_at timestamp remains unchanged as historical record.

Attachment management supports adding new files/images via attachments_to_add field and removing existing attachments via attachments_to_remove field. File additions are validated before acceptance. Attachment removals immediately delete files from storage. Maximum article constraints remain enforced: 10 total attachments, 100 MB combined size.

Authorization is enforced: members can only update articles they created (matching discussion_board_member_id), while moderators can update any article regardless of authorship. The system rejects unauthorized updates with permission denied errors.

Permissions for updates:
- Title: Can be updated by article author or moderators
- Content: Can be updated by article author or moderators
- Category: Can be updated by article author or moderators (though some business rules may restrict category changes)
- Attachments: Can be added/removed by article author or moderators

Articles that have been soft-deleted (deleted_at is not NULL) cannot be updated and will return a not found or deleted status error.

id.description: Unique identifier for the member. System-generated UUID that uniquely identifies this member across the discussion board platform.

email.description: Member's email address used for authentication and account identification. Unique across all members. Used in attribution displays and for account management references.

account_status.description: Current status of the member account. Valid values: 'active' (normal operation), 'suspended' (temporary access denial, typically 7 days), 'banned' (permanent access denial). Indicates whether the member can create content and interact with the platform.

created_at.description: Timestamp when the member account was created in ISO 8601 UTC format. System-generated at registration and immutable thereafter. Used for audit trails and account age tracking.

updated_at.description: Timestamp when the member account was last modified in ISO 8601 UTC format. Updated whenever account details change. Tracks the most recent account modification for audit purposes.

IDiscussionBoardMember.ISummary.description: Lightweight summary representation of a member containing essential identifying information. This summary includes the member's unique ID, email address for identification, and current account status. Member status is important for understanding member state: 'active' members are in good standing, 'suspended' members have temporary access restrictions, and 'banned' members are permanently blocked. Member summaries are used throughout the platform for attribution (showing who created articles or comments), author identification in discussion threads, and notifications about member actions. The summary provides sufficient information for user identification without exposing sensitive account details. Email address is included for identification purposes in user lists and attribution displays.

id.description: Unique identifier for the category. Primary key generated by the system as UUID.

code.description: Unique category code/identifier used throughout the system (e.g., 'economics', 'politics'). This is the programmatic identifier for the category used in filtering and organization.

name.description: Human-readable category name displayed to users (e.g., 'Economics', 'Politics'). This is what users see when selecting or filtering by category in the user interface.

description.description: Optional detailed description of the category explaining its scope and purpose. Helps users understand which category is appropriate for their content. Null if no description provided.

displayOrder.description: Numeric ordering value for displaying categories in UI. Lower numbers appear first in lists and navigation menus. Allows flexible category ordering without requiring alphabetical sort.

isActive.description: Flag indicating whether the category is currently active and available for new article creation. Inactive categories can still be queried for existing articles but are hidden from category selection in UI.

createdAt.description: Timestamp when the category was created or added to the system. Stored in ISO 8601 UTC format for audit trail purposes. System-generated, immutable.

updatedAt.description: Timestamp when the category was last modified. Updated whenever category metadata changes (name, description, display order, active status). Stored in ISO 8601 UTC format.

deletedAt.description: Timestamp when the category was soft-deleted (retired from use). Null for active categories. Soft deletion preserves referential integrity - articles can still reference deleted categories for historical accuracy. Stored in ISO 8601 UTC format.

IDiscussionBoardCategory.description: System reference table defining article categories for the discussion board platform. Provides canonical set of allowed category values (Economics, Politics) that articles must be classified under. This is a system-managed configuration table, not user-created. Categories represent the fundamental classification system for organizing discussions. All articles must belong to exactly one category. The category system enables content discovery, filtering by topic, and organization of discussions into topic domains.

page.description: Page number for pagination starting from 1. Used with limit to retrieve specific pages of results. Default is 1 if not specified. Must be a positive integer. Used in offset calculation as (page - 1) * limit.

limit.description: Number of comments per page for pagination. Default is 20 if not specified. Maximum allowed is 100 comments per page to prevent excessive data transfer. Must be a positive integer between 1 and 100.

search.description: Full-text search keywords to find comments matching specific content. Searches across comment text content and author names. Uses stemming to match variations (e.g., 'discuss', 'discussing', 'discussion' all match). Multiple keywords use OR logic (any keyword match returns result). Optional parameter; if omitted, searches all comments.

sort_by.description: Field to sort results by. Valid values: 'created_at' (creation timestamp), 'updated_at' (modification timestamp), 'reply_count' (number of replies to this comment), 'relevance' (for search results). Default is 'created_at' if not specified. Determines primary sort order for results.

order.description: Sort direction: 'asc' (ascending, oldest first for dates, lowest count first) or 'desc' (descending, newest first for dates, highest count first). Default is 'desc' if not specified. Applied to the field specified in sort_by.

status.description: Filter comments by current status. Valid values: 'published' (active comments), 'deleted' (soft-deleted by author), 'moderated' (removed by moderators). Can filter by single status or all statuses. Visibility rules still apply based on user role (guests/members cannot see moderated content details).

article_id.description: Optional filter to retrieve only comments on a specific article. If provided, results limited to comments under the specified article ID. If omitted, searches across all articles the user can access.

parent_comment_id.description: Optional filter to retrieve only replies to a specific parent comment (showing nested discussion thread). If provided, results limited to comments with this parent_comment_id. If omitted, includes both top-level comments and replies.

author_id.description: Optional filter to retrieve only comments authored by a specific member. Useful for viewing one member's contributions or in member profile contexts. If omitted, includes comments from all authors.

created_after.description: Optional filter to retrieve only comments created after this timestamp (ISO 8601 UTC format). Used for finding recent comments or comments within date ranges. If omitted, includes comments from any creation date.

created_before.description: Optional filter to retrieve only comments created before this timestamp (ISO 8601 UTC format). Used with created_after to define date ranges. If omitted, includes comments up to current time.

IDiscussionBoardComment.IRequest.description:
Search criteria and pagination parameters for filtering, sorting, and retrieving comments from discussion threads.

This request DTO enables comprehensive search and discovery of comments across articles. Members and guests can filter comments by content keywords, author, creation date ranges, and moderation status. The operation supports pagination with configurable page sizes and multiple sorting options including creation date (newest/oldest first), reply count (most discussed first), and relevance for search queries.

Pagination is managed through page and limit parameters with sensible defaults (page 1, limit 20 comments per page). The operation supports offset-based pagination allowing users to navigate through large result sets efficiently. For search operations, keyword matching uses full-text search across comment content and author names with stemming support (e.g., 'discuss', 'discussing', 'discussion' all match).

Filtering capabilities include status filtering (published, deleted, moderated), date range filtering (comments created between start_date and end_date), and author filtering (comments by specific members). Sorting options include chronological ordering (oldest first, newest first), relevance ranking for search queries, and reply count ordering (most replied first).

Rate limiting is enforced on search requests: maximum 100 search requests per hour per authenticated user. Visibility rules are automatically applied based on user role (guest/member/moderator) without requiring explicit filtering parameters. The request DTO preserves user input for error recovery when validation fails.

content.description: The comment text body containing the member's discussion contribution. Between 1 and 5,000 characters in length. Cannot be empty or contain only whitespace. Supports plain text and basic markdown formatting (bold, italic, links). All URLs in the content are validated for protocol (HTTP/HTTPS) and against security blocklists. This is the primary content field - all other fields are optional.

parent_comment_id.description: Optional reference to a parent comment if this is a reply within a threaded discussion. If provided, this comment is a response to the specified parent comment and will be nested under it in the thread structure. If omitted (null/undefined), this is a top-level comment posted directly to the article. The parent comment must exist and belong to the same article. Thread depth is automatically calculated and limited to 3 levels maximum.

attachments.description: Optional array of file attachments to include with the comment. Maximum 5 files per comment with combined size not exceeding 10 MB total. Each attachment is validated for file type (supported: JPEG, PNG, GIF, WebP for images; PDF, DOCX, TXT for documents), size, and security (malware scanning). Attachments are processed server-side before comment publication.

IDiscussionBoardComment.ICreate.description:
Request data for creating a new comment or reply on an article.

This DTO enables members to post comments directly on articles or as replies to existing comments. All comments are published immediately without moderation approval. The operation validates content meets quality standards (1-5000 characters minimum), checks authentication and account status, verifies the target article is published (not deleted or archived), and applies rate limiting (maximum 50 comments per member per hour).

Comments can include optional file attachments (images or documents). Maximum 5 files per comment, combined size not exceeding 10 MB. Attachments are validated for file type, size, and security (malware scanning) before acceptance. Optional attachment descriptions/captions can accompany each file.

For reply comments, the parent_comment_id field must reference an existing comment on the same article. When creating a reply, the system automatically handles thread depth calculation (0 for top-level, 1+ for nested replies, maximum depth 3). The authenticated member becomes the comment author automatically (not provided in request).

Comment text supports basic markdown formatting (bold, italic, links). Plain text is also accepted. The system validates all URLs in comment text against a security blocklist and validates URL protocols (HTTP/HTTPS only). Duplicate detection prevents near-identical comments within 24-hour windows with user warning if detected.

Upon successful creation, the comment is immediately visible in the article's comment thread (or nested under parent comment if a reply). If the comment is a reply, the parent comment author is notified. The comment's creation timestamp and edit history tracking are initialized by the system.

IDiscussionBoardComment.description:
Complete comment entity with all metadata, content, and current state information. Returned after comment creation, updates, or moderation actions. Includes comment identification, authorship information, content body, threading information (parent comment reference and reply count), and moderation status.

Comments support nested replies up to 3 levels deep through optional parent_comment_id field, allowing creation of discussion threads. The status field indicates visibility: 'published' comments are visible to all users, 'moderated' comments are hidden from regular users showing '[Removed by moderator]' instead. Edit count tracks how many times the comment has been modified by its author. Thread depth indicates nesting level for visual rendering. Reply count indicates how many direct replies have been posted to this comment, essential for understanding nested discussion depth.

This full IDiscussionBoardComment type provides complete information for detailed comment display, whereas the ISummary variant provides lightweight representation for use in comment lists and discussion threads.

id.description: Unique identifier of the comment. System-generated UUID that serves as the primary key. Used throughout the platform for referencing this specific comment in URLs, relationships, and API operations.

discussion_board_article_id.description: Unique identifier of the parent article this comment belongs to. Foreign key reference to discussion_board_articles.id. Every comment is associated with exactly one article. Used to link comments to their parent discussion context and enable navigation between comments and articles.

discussion_board_member_id.description: Unique identifier of the member who authored this comment. Foreign key reference to discussion_board_members.id. Identifies the comment author throughout the system. Used for attribution, permission checks, and notification purposes.

parent_comment_id.description: Unique identifier of the parent comment if this comment is a reply to another comment. Foreign key reference to discussion_board_comments.id for self-referential relationship. Null for top-level comments posted directly on articles. Enables nested discussion threading up to 3 levels deep. Used for visual hierarchical display and thread context preservation.

content.description: The comment text body containing user's discussion contribution. Between 1 and 5,000 characters. Supports basic markdown formatting (bold, italic, links). Contains the substantive comment content that participates in the article discussion.

status.description: Current publication and moderation status of the comment. Valid values: 'published' (visible to all users), 'moderated' (hidden from public view, marked as removed by moderator), 'deleted' (soft-deleted by author). Determines visibility in comment threads and search results. Updated when moderators or authors take actions on the comment.

thread_depth.description: Nesting level in the discussion thread. 0 for top-level comments directly on articles, 1 for replies to top-level comments, 2 for replies to depth-1 comments. Maximum nesting is 3 levels. Used for visual indentation and thread structure rendering in the UI.

reply_count.description: Number of direct replies posted to this comment. Shows how many members have responded directly to this specific comment, indicating discussion engagement on this particular comment thread. Essential for rendering nested discussion structure and highlighting active sub-threads. Incremented when new replies are created, decremented when replies are deleted.

edit_count.description: Number of times this comment has been edited by its author. Starts at 0 when comment is created. Incremented each time author modifies the comment. Used to display 'edited' indicator to users and track comment edit history.

created_at.description: Timestamp when the comment was initially created. Set once at creation and never changes even if comment is edited. Stored in ISO 8601 UTC format. Used for chronological ordering of comments in threads and audit trail purposes.

updated_at.description: Timestamp of the most recent modification to the comment. Updated whenever comment text or other fields change. Stored in ISO 8601 UTC format. Allows tracking when comments were last modified.

deleted_at.description: Soft delete timestamp indicating when the comment was removed or archived. Stored in ISO 8601 UTC format. Null indicates the comment is active. Set when user deletes comment or moderator removes comment. Preserves audit trail while allowing soft deletion and recovery.

author.description: The member who created the comment. Includes author's name and basic profile information. Provides complete attribution for the comment. Used to allow users to click through to author's profile for discovering other comments they've written.

article.description: The article this comment belongs to. Provides context about which article is being discussed and enables navigation to the parent article. References the article being commented on. Essential for understanding discussion context.

parent_comment.description: The parent comment if this is a reply to another comment. Null for top-level comments. Enables nested discussion threading by linking replies to their parent comment. Allows visual representation of discussion hierarchy and conversation context.

id.description: Unique identifier for the comment. System-generated UUID that uniquely identifies this specific comment within the discussion board.

discussion_board_article_id.description: Reference to the parent article this comment belongs to. Foreign key to discussion_board_articles.id. Indicates which article discussion this comment participates in.

author.description: The member who authored this comment. Contains summary information about the comment author including their ID and basic profile details. Essential for attribution and user identification in discussions.

content.description: The comment text body containing the user's discussion contribution. Between 1 and 5,000 characters. Represents the substantive content of the comment in the discussion thread.

status.description: Current status of the comment. Valid values: 'published' (visible and active), 'deleted' (removed by author, marked as deleted), 'moderated' (removed by moderator for policy violation). Controls visibility and moderation state.

thread_depth.description: Nesting level in the discussion thread. 0 for top-level comments posted directly on articles, 1+ for replies to other comments. Maximum depth is 3 levels. Indicates position in the nested comment hierarchy.

created_at.description: Timestamp when the comment was created. Stored in ISO 8601 UTC format. Used for chronological ordering of comments and discussion threads.

updated_at.description: Timestamp when the comment was last modified. Stored in ISO 8601 UTC format. Updated when comment text is edited by the author or modified by moderators. Indicates whether comment has been changed after initial creation.

edit_count.description: Number of times this comment has been edited by its author. Starts at 0. Incremented each time author modifies the comment. Used to display 'edited' indicator to users showing comment has been modified.

IDiscussionBoardComment.ISummary.description:
Lightweight summary representation of a comment optimized for display in comment lists and discussion threads.

This summary includes essential comment information needed for rendering comments in discussion views: the comment text, author attribution, thread position, and temporal metadata. The summary includes the full comment text (not truncated) to provide context in the discussion thread.

The author information is provided as a member summary containing identification and basic profile details. The thread_depth field indicates the nesting level in the discussion (0 for top-level, 1+ for replies), enabling proper visual hierarchical display.

The status field communicates visibility state: 'published' comments are fully visible, 'deleted' comments show as removed by author, and 'moderated' comments show as removed by moderators. The edit_count indicates if the comment was modified after creation, allowing users to see that comments have been edited.

This summary type is used for displaying comments in article discussions, user comment histories, and search results where complete comment information is needed for user understanding.

content.description:
Updated comment text body. Between 1 and 5,000 characters in length. Only the comment content can be modified through this operation. Author, creation date, parent comment reference, and article association remain immutable.

Validation requires content be non-empty and contain meaningful text - cannot be only whitespace or special characters. The system increments edit_count and updates the modified timestamp when this field is changed.

change_reason.description: Optional reason for the update, particularly used by moderators to document why they edited a comment. Maximum 500 characters. Used for transparency when moderators modify content. Regular members typically do not provide a reason for their own edits.

IDiscussionBoardComment.IUpdate.description:
Request body for updating an existing comment's content text.

Allows members to modify their own comments within 24 hours of creation. Moderators can edit any comment at any time with optional reason documentation for transparency. The update operation preserves all structural information (author, creation date, parent reference, article association) and only modifies the content text.

Validation includes checking content length (1-5000 characters), confirming content is not empty or meaningless, and for members ensuring the 24-hour edit window has not elapsed. The system increments edit_count and updates the modification timestamp upon successful update.

IDiscussionBoardAttachment.description:
Complete attachment (file or image) metadata and reference information.

Represents a file or image attachment associated with an article or comment. Includes metadata for display, download, and security status. Used in article and comment responses to show associated files and images.

Supports polymorphic attachment to either articles or comments through attachable_type discriminator pattern. Images are displayed inline in content, while documents are provided as downloadable links. All attachments go through security scanning (malware detection) before being made available to users.

Stores file metadata (name, size, type, dimensions for images) and security status. Image attachments have thumbnail and optimized versions generated for efficient display. All file access is tracked for audit purposes.

id.description: Unique identifier for the attachment assigned by the system. System-generated UUID used to uniquely identify this attachment record across the platform.

discussion_board_member_id.description: Unique identifier of the member who uploaded the attachment. Foreign key reference to discussion_board_members.id. Identifies who contributed the file and enables permission checking for attachment management.

discussion_board_article_id.description: Unique identifier of the article this attachment belongs to if attachable_type is 'article'. Foreign key reference to discussion_board_articles.id. Null if this attachment belongs to a comment instead. Used for determining polymorphic attachment target and relationship management.

discussion_board_comment_id.description: Unique identifier of the comment this attachment belongs to if attachable_type is 'comment'. Foreign key reference to discussion_board_comments.id. Null if this attachment belongs to an article instead. Used for determining polymorphic attachment target and relationship management.

attachable_type.description: Type of parent content this attachment belongs to. Valid values: 'article' (attachment is part of article content) or 'comment' (attachment is part of comment content). Discriminator field used to determine which foreign key is active (article_id vs comment_id). Application must validate this matches the non-null FK field.

filename.description: Original filename provided by the uploader. Sanitized to remove path traversal sequences and special characters for safe storage. Displayed to users and used for download operations. Preserves user-provided filename for reference.

file_type.description: MIME type of the file (e.g., 'image/jpeg', 'application/pdf'). Indicates how the attachment should be handled (displayed inline for images, downloaded for documents). Validated during upload to match actual file content.

file_extension.description: File extension without leading dot (e.g., 'jpg', 'pdf'). Extracted from filename and validated against list of 19 supported extensions. Must correspond with file_type MIME classification for consistency. Used for quick format identification.

file_size.description: Size of the file in bytes. Validated during upload against platform limits: images 10 MB maximum (10485760 bytes), documents 20 MB maximum (20971520 bytes), archives 50 MB maximum (52428800 bytes). Used for quota tracking and displayed to users for download size indication.

storage_path.description: Unique server-side storage path or identifier where the file is physically stored. UUID or hash-based to guarantee uniqueness. Never exposed to users in responses. Used internally for file retrieval, access control, and deletion operations.

image_width.description: Width of the image in pixels if this is an image attachment. Null for non-image attachments (documents, archives). Extracted during image processing and validation. Used for responsive image rendering and aspect ratio preservation.

image_height.description: Height of the image in pixels if this is an image attachment. Null for non-image attachments. Extracted during image processing and validation. Used for responsive image rendering calculations.

security_status.description: Security validation status of the attachment file. Valid values: 'pending_scan' (awaiting malware scan completion), 'safe' (antivirus scan passed, file cleared for serving), 'infected' (malware detected in file), 'quarantined' (file isolated due to security violation). Determines whether attachment can be displayed, downloaded, or must be hidden from users.

malware_scan_result.description: Detailed result from antivirus/malware scanning if performed. Null if scan is pending or not yet performed. Contains specific threat information from scanning service (e.g., 'detected: trojan.xyz') when malware is found. Only populated when scanning is completed with non-null result.

created_at.description: Timestamp when the attachment was uploaded in ISO 8601 UTC format. System-generated at upload completion. Used for audit trail, chronological ordering of attachments, and storage lifecycle tracking.

updated_at.description: Timestamp when the attachment metadata was last modified. Updated when security scan results change, filename is updated, or other metadata changes. Stored in ISO 8601 UTC format. Critical for tracking when files transitioned to safe status or were flagged as threats.

deleted_at.description: Soft delete timestamp indicating when the attachment was removed or archived. Stored in ISO 8601 UTC format. Null indicates the attachment is active and visible. Set when user deletes attachment or parent article/comment is deleted. Preserves audit trail while enabling recovery.

download_url.description: Computed/generated URL for downloading or viewing the attachment. This field is generated at response time based on the attachment's storage_path and security_status, not stored in the Prisma database schema. For images with security_status='safe', the URL links to the optimized web version. For documents with security_status='safe', the URL links to the downloadable file. Only populated/accessible for attachments with security_status='safe'. Generated by the application layer based on storage configuration. Null or omitted if attachment has not passed security scanning yet.

page.description: Page number for pagination (1-based indexing). Specifies which page of results to retrieve. Default is page 1.

limit.description: Number of attachment records to return per page. Default is typically 20. Maximum 100 to prevent excessive data retrieval.

search.description: Search query to filter attachments by filename or other searchable properties. Case-insensitive keyword matching across filename and MIME type. Optional - omit to retrieve all attachments.

file_type.description: Filter attachments by MIME type (e.g., 'image/jpeg', 'application/pdf'). Optional - omit to include all file types. Can be used to show only images or only documents.

security_status.description: Filter attachments by security validation status. Valid values: 'pending_scan', 'safe', 'infected', 'quarantined'. Optional - omit to include all security statuses. Useful for viewing potentially problematic files.

sort_by.description: Field to sort results by. Valid values: 'filename', 'created_at', 'file_size', 'security_status'. Default is 'created_at'. Determines attachment list ordering.

sort_order.description: Sort direction: 'asc' for ascending (oldest/smallest first) or 'desc' for descending (newest/largest first). Default is 'desc' for created_at, 'asc' for other fields.

IDiscussionBoardAttachment.IRequest.description:
Search criteria, filtering options, and pagination parameters for retrieving attachments

Enables clients to search, filter, and paginate through the list of attachments attached to a specific article. All parameters are optional, allowing flexible query construction.

Supports pagination through page and limit parameters. Search filters by filename. File type and security status filters allow narrowing results by classification. Sorting enables customizable result ordering by filename, upload date, file size, or security status.

Used for the PATCH /articles/{articleId}/attachments endpoint to retrieve filtered and paginated attachment lists.

content.description: The raw binary file content being downloaded. Transmitted as application/octet-stream MIME type. The actual file bytes served to the client for download or display. For image files (JPEG, PNG, GIF, WebP), the browser will typically display inline. For document files (PDF, Word, Excel, archives), the browser will trigger download behavior with the original filename.

filename.description: Original sanitized filename for the downloaded file. Used in the HTTP Content-Disposition header to specify the filename when the browser saves the file. Example: 'economic-report-2024.pdf' or 'chart.jpg'.

file_type.description: MIME type of the file being served. Used in the HTTP Content-Type header to instruct the browser how to handle the file. Examples: 'image/jpeg' for JPG files (display inline), 'application/pdf' for PDF files (may display or download depending on browser settings), 'application/zip' for archive files (download).

file_size.description: Size of the file in bytes. Provided for informational purposes and used in HTTP Content-Length header for progress indication. Allows clients to estimate download time and validate complete file receipt.

IBinaryFileResponse.description:
Response body for file download operations returning the raw file content and metadata.

This DTO wraps the binary file content being downloaded along with essential metadata for proper browser handling. The content field contains the actual file bytes as application/octet-stream. The HTTP response includes appropriate headers: Content-Type set to file_type (image/jpeg, application/pdf, etc.), Content-Disposition set to attachment or inline based on file type, and Content-Length set to file_size for accurate progress indication.

Image files (JPEG, PNG, GIF, WebP) are served with MIME types that allow browser inline display. Document files (PDF, Word, Excel, archives) are served to trigger download dialogs with the sanitized filename. The file_type metadata allows clients to handle different file types appropriately and determine whether to display or save the file.

This response type is used for the file download endpoint that retrieves attachment content from storage and serves it to authenticated or guest users based on access permissions.

id.description: Unique identifier of the attachment being validated for security status.

security_status.description:
Current security validation status of the attachment file.

Possible values:
- 'pending_scan': File is awaiting antivirus/malware scanning
- 'safe': File has passed security scan and is clean for download
- 'infected': Malware or malicious content detected in file
- 'quarantined': File isolated due to security or policy violation

Governs whether attachment can be displayed, downloaded, or must be hidden from users.

malware_scan_result.description:
Detailed result from antivirus/malware scanning if the file has been scanned.

Contains specific threat information from the security scanner (e.g., 'detected: trojan.xyz'). Only populated when scan is completed and has completed successfully or detected threats. NULL if scan is pending or file has not yet been scanned.

Used by the application to provide detailed security information to moderators and to determine file handling policy.

filename.description: Original filename provided by uploader. Used for display and download. Sanitized to remove path traversal sequences and special characters.

file_type.description: MIME type of the file (e.g., 'image/jpeg', 'application/pdf'). Validated during upload against supported types. Used for security classification and display handling.

file_extension.description: File extension without dot (e.g., 'jpg', 'pdf'). Extracted from filename and validated against list of 19 supported extensions. Must match file_type MIME classification.

file_size.description: Size of file in bytes. Validated against limits during upload: images 10MB max, documents 20MB max, archives 50MB max. Stored for audit trail and quota tracking.

created_at.description: Timestamp when attachment was uploaded (ISO 8601 UTC). Used for audit trail and storage lifecycle tracking.

IDiscussionBoardAttachment.ISecurityStat.description:
Security validation status and metadata for an attachment file.

This DTO represents the current security state of an attachment, indicating whether the file has passed antivirus/malware scanning and is safe for display and download. Used by the application UI to determine file handling and by moderators to review security validation results.

The security_status field indicates the validation state: 'pending_scan' (awaiting scan), 'safe' (clean for download), 'infected' (malware detected, cannot download), or 'quarantined' (isolated due to violation). The malware_scan_result field provides detailed threat information if scanning has been completed.

This DTO includes sufficient metadata (filename, file_type, file_size, created_at) for proper file identification and audit purposes.

IDiscussionBoardCommentModeration.IUpdat.description:
Request body for moderator review and moderation action on comments. Moderators use this DTO to approve, remove, or restore comments. The operation updates comment status (published/moderated/deleted) and creates corresponding moderation log entries for audit trails. When removing comments, the status changes to 'moderated' making the content hidden while preserving the comment record for thread integrity and audit purposes. When approving comments, the status is set to 'published' and any flags are cleared.

The action_type field is required and determines the moderation outcome: 'approve' clears flags and restores visibility, 'remove' hides content from regular users while preserving the record, 'restore' reverses previous moderation. The reason field is optional but recommended for transparency, documenting why the moderator took this action for the comment author and audit trail purposes. All moderation actions are logged immutably in discussion_board_moderation_logs for compliance tracking.

action_type.description: Type of moderation action to take on the comment. Valid values are: 'approve' (clear flags and set status to published), 'remove' (mark as moderated and hide content from regular users), or 'restore' (restore previously moderated comment). This field determines how the comment status will be updated and what moderation log entry is created. Required to specify the intended moderation outcome.

reason.description: Moderator-provided explanation for the moderation action taken. Optional detailed reason explaining why the comment was approved, removed, or restored. Should reference specific community guideline violations when applicable. Supports transparency by documenting the basis for moderation decisions. Maximum 500 characters. Displayed to comment author and recorded in moderation audit log.

IDiscussionBoardArticle.ISummary.description:
Lightweight summary representation of an article optimized for list views and article discovery. Contains essential information for displaying articles in listing pages and search results without full content. Summary DTOs are used in article lists and pagination contexts where full article detail would be inefficient.

Summary articles provide quick scanning information including title, author, dates, and engagement metrics (views, comment count). Used in article listing pages, search results, and anywhere articles are displayed in lists rather than full detail views. Summary format omits the full article content body to keep responses efficient. All Prisma fields referenced are directly mapped from discussion_board_articles table: id (primary key), title (3-200 characters), createdAt (creation timestamp), updatedAt (modification timestamp), viewCount (view counter), status (published/archived indicator), category (foreign key to discussion_board_categories), author (foreign key to discussion_board_members via discussion_board_member_id), and commentCount (derived from comment count on article).

id.description: Unique identifier for the article. Primary key generated by the system as UUID.

title.description: Article title between 3 and 200 characters. Displayed in article listings and article header. Primary text users see when browsing for articles.

createdAt.description: Timestamp when the article was initially created. Set once at creation and never changes even if article is edited. Stored in ISO 8601 UTC format for accurate publication dating.

updatedAt.description: Timestamp of most recent modification. Updated whenever article title, content, or other fields change. Stored in ISO 8601 UTC format. Allows users to see when article was last edited.

viewCount.description: Number of times the article has been viewed. Incremented on each unique user view within 24-hour deduplication window. Used to track article popularity and engagement. Non-negative integer.

status.description: Current article state: 'published' for visible articles, 'archived' for moderator-hidden articles. Determines visibility to users. Articles in archived state are hidden from public view.

category.description: The category this article belongs to (Economics or Politics). Required for all articles. Uses full category object for complete context about article's classification.

author.description: Member who created the article. Contains author information including name/identifier. Essential context for attributing article to its creator.

commentCount.description: Number of comments posted on this article. Used in article listing to show discussion activity level. Helps users identify active discussions.

IPagination.description:
Standard pagination metadata included in paginated responses.

This DTO provides information about the current page, total pages, total items, and items per page to enable client-side pagination controls and user awareness of result set size.

page.description: Current page number (1-indexed). The page of results that is currently being displayed.

limit.description: Number of records per page. How many items are included in each page of results.

total.description: Total number of records across all pages. Complete count of all matching records without pagination.

total_pages.description: Total number of pages available. Calculated from total records divided by limit per page. Helps determine if there are more pages to retrieve.

violation_summary.description: Summary statistics about user policy violations on the platform. Includes total violations recorded since platform inception, count of members with violations, count of members approaching automatic suspension threshold (3+ violations in last 30 days), count of members approaching automatic permanent ban threshold (5+ violations in last 90 days), violations recorded this calendar month for trend analysis, and breakdown of violations by type showing which violation categories are most prevalent. Enables rapid assessment of violation trends and enforcement workload.

recent_moderation_actions.description: Array of the 20 most recent moderation actions taken by any moderator on the platform. Each entry provides complete audit trail of enforcement decision including moderator who took action (moderator_id, moderator email), action_type taken (remove_article, remove_comment, suspend_user, ban_user, restore_article, restore_comment, warning_issued, flag_content), target_type (article, comment, member) and target_id identifying specific affected entity, timestamp when action was executed, and reason provided by moderator documenting rationale for action. Ordered by creation timestamp, most recent first. Enables tracking and auditing of recent enforcement activities and moderator decision patterns.

pending_content_review.description: Summary of articles and comments currently pending moderator review or enforcement decision. Includes counts of flagged articles and flagged comments awaiting moderator action, total count of pending items requiring review, and timestamp of the oldest pending item still awaiting decision. Enables moderators to identify content items that require enforcement decisions and prioritize review of long-standing flagged items.

active_suspensions.description: Count of user accounts currently under temporary suspension, unable to authenticate or create content until suspension expires. These members have account_status = 'suspended' with a future expiration timestamp. Used to assess current account restrictions in effect and estimate enforcement volume. Suspended members can typically appeal or wait for suspension period to automatically expire (usually 7 days).

permanent_bans.description: Count of user accounts permanently banned from the platform, with no ability to access system or create new accounts. These members have account_status = 'banned' with no expiration. Permanent bans are not automatically reversible and require explicit administrator intervention to reinstate. Indicates scale of severe enforcement actions taken against most problematic users.

total_violations_recorded.description: Total cumulative count of policy violations recorded across all members since platform inception. Includes all violation records in discussion_board_user_violations table regardless of whether violations triggered suspensions, bans, or just warnings. Indicates total enforcement volume across platform history and helps contextualize current violation trends within historical baselines.

moderation_actions_this_month.description: Count of moderation actions taken by any moderator during the current calendar month. Includes all action_type values (remove_article, remove_comment, suspend_user, ban_user, restore_article, restore_comment, warning_issued, flag_content). Used to assess current moderation workload this period and identify enforcement trend this month compared to historical monthly baselines. Helps identify seasonal patterns or sudden spikes in enforcement volume.

IDiscussionBoardModerationDashboard.description:
Comprehensive moderation dashboard aggregating key metrics, recent actions, and content review queues. Provides moderators with unified administrative oversight of platform moderation activities, user violations, and pending content items requiring review.

The dashboard aggregates data from multiple tables to present key sections: violation tracking showing users approaching automatic enforcement thresholds (3 violations within 30 days triggers 7-day account suspension, 5 violations within 90 days triggers permanent account ban), recent moderation actions taken by any moderator with full audit trail, pending content flagged for review (articles and comments with status other than 'published'), and platform moderation statistics including total violations recorded, active suspensions, and enforcement trends.

Moderation enforcement operates on a tiered violation system. Violations are recorded in the discussion_board_user_violations table with violation_type (spam, harassment, inappropriate_content, off_topic, misinformation, copyright_violation, illegal_content), violation_date for threshold calculations, and links to associated moderation_log_id when enforcement action is taken. Automatic enforcement triggers when violation thresholds are exceeded. All actions are recorded in discussion_board_moderation_logs with complete audit trail including moderator_id (who took action), action_type (remove_article, remove_comment, suspend_user, ban_user, restore_article, restore_comment, warning_issued, flag_content), target_type (article, comment, member) with polymorphic targeting, timestamp of action, and reason documenting rationale.

Content status tracking uses discussion_board_articles.status and discussion_board_comments.status: 'published' indicates active visible content, 'archived' indicates moderator-hidden articles, 'deleted' indicates user or moderator deletion, 'moderated' indicates content removed by moderators. Dashboard displays all non-published content and provides controls for moderators to review, restore, or permanently delete flagged items.

This dashboard enables rapid assessment of platform moderation state, identification of problematic users through cumulative violation patterns, content review for policy compliance, and tracking of enforcement actions for compliance and transparency purposes. The operation requires moderator authentication and is not accessible to regular members or guests.

id.description: Unique identifier for the notification record. System-generated UUID used to identify and reference this specific notification throughout the platform.

recipient_member_id.description: Reference to the member who is the recipient of this notification. The authenticated member who should receive and view this notification about the triggering event.

triggering_article_id.description: Optional reference to the article that triggered this notification if applicable. Present when notification is about article comments, article moderation, or other article-related events. NULL if notification is not article-related.

triggering_comment_id.description: Optional reference to the comment that triggered this notification if applicable. Present when notification is about comment replies, comment moderation, or other comment-related events. NULL if notification is not comment-related.

source_member_id.description: Optional reference to the member who caused or triggered this notification if applicable. The user who commented, mentioned, or triggered the event that generated this notification. NULL if notification was system-generated without a specific source member.

notification_type.description: Type of notification event that triggered this notification. Valid values: 'comment_reply' (someone replied to user's comment), 'mention' (user was mentioned in comment), 'article_moderation' (user's article was moderated/removed), 'comment_moderation' (user's comment was moderated/removed). Categorizes what event triggered this notification for filtering and display purposes.

title.description: Short title or subject of the notification for display in notification lists and headers. Examples: 'New reply to your comment', 'Your article was removed', 'You were mentioned'. Kept brief (50-100 characters) for quick scanning by users.

message.description: Full notification message body providing detailed context about the event. Includes information about what happened, who it was from (if applicable), and relevant article/comment information. Supports markdown or plain text formatting (typically 200-500 characters).

is_read.description: Whether the user has read or viewed this notification. False indicates unread notification that should be visually highlighted in user's notification inbox. Used for tracking user engagement with notifications and calculating unread notification counts.

read_at.description: ISO 8601 UTC timestamp when the user read or viewed this notification. NULL if notification has not been read yet (is_read = false). Updated automatically when user marks notification as read. Used for tracking engagement timing and sorting notifications.

action_url.description: Optional URL or deep link to navigate directly to the related content when notification is clicked. Examples: '/articles/[articleId]#comment-[commentId]' for comment reply notifications or '/articles/[articleId]' for article-related notifications. NULL for notifications without a direct action target.

email_sent_at.description: ISO 8601 UTC timestamp when this notification was sent via email to the recipient member. NULL if notification has not been emailed yet or if user has email notifications disabled. Used to track which notifications have been delivered via email and for email retry logic.

email_failed_at.description: ISO 8601 UTC timestamp when email delivery for this notification failed. NULL if email was sent successfully or notification was not attempted to be sent via email. Used to track failed email deliveries for retry and debugging.

email_send_error.description: Error message or reason code if email delivery failed. NULL if email sent successfully or was not attempted. Examples: 'SMTP_TIMEOUT', 'INVALID_ADDRESS', 'BOUNCE'. Enables troubleshooting of email delivery failures and support escalation.

recipient_email.description: Email address of the recipient member at the time of notification creation. Denormalized from member record for efficient email delivery without additional database queries. NULL if member has no email address or email delivery is disabled. Allows sending emails even if member record is subsequently updated.

created_at.description: ISO 8601 UTC timestamp when this notification was created and generated. Marks when the triggering event occurred in the system. System-generated and immutable. Used for chronological sorting (newest first) and for notification cleanup policies.

updated_at.description: ISO 8601 UTC timestamp when this notification record was last modified. Updated when notification status changes (marked read, email sent, etc.). Used for audit trail tracking and monitoring notification lifecycle changes.

deleted_at.description: ISO 8601 UTC timestamp when this notification was deleted/archived by the user. NULL indicates active notification. Used for soft deletion allowing recovery and maintains audit trail of user actions on notifications. Deleted notifications are hidden from user's notification inbox.

IDiscussionBoardNotification.description:
A notification record informing a member about relevant events such as comment replies, mentions, and moderation actions. Each notification represents a discrete event requiring user awareness and support independent user workflows including browsing, marking as read, and deletion.

Notifications can be triggered by various events: when another member replies to a user's comment, when a user is mentioned in a comment, when a moderator removes a user's article, or when a user's comment is removed by a moderator.

Each notification contains context about what triggered it (triggering_article_id, triggering_comment_id, source_member_id) to enable users to quickly navigate to the related content. The notification_type field categorizes the event for filtering and display. Users can interact with notifications by marking them as read/unread or soft-deleting them from their inbox (setting deleted_at timestamp).

Notifications also support email delivery tracking with email_sent_at, email_failed_at, and email_send_error fields for monitoring notification delivery to user email addresses.

page.description: Page number for pagination (1-indexed). Defaults to 1 if not specified. Used to control which set of notifications are returned when results exceed page size.

limit.description: Number of notifications to return per page. Maximum 100 to prevent excessive data transfer. Defaults to 20 if not specified. Controls the page size for notification list retrieval.

notification_type.description: Optional filter to return only notifications of a specific type. Valid values: 'comment_reply', 'mention', 'article_moderation', 'comment_moderation'. NULL or omitted means return all notification types.

is_read.description: Optional filter to return only notifications with specific read status. True returns only read notifications, False returns only unread notifications. NULL or omitted means return both read and unread notifications.

search.description: Optional full-text search query to find notifications by title or message content. Uses trigram indexes for efficient matching. NULL or omitted means no search filtering. Searches across title and message fields with relevance ranking.

oneOf.description: Field to sort notifications by. Valid values: 'created_at' (notification creation time, newest first), 'read_at' (when notification was read, most recent reads first), 'updated_at' (last modification time, newest first). Defaults to 'created_at' if not specified.

Field to sort notifications by. Valid values: 'created_at' (notification creation time, newest first), 'read_at' (when notification was read, most recent reads first), 'updated_at' (last modification time, newest first). Defaults to 'created_at' if not specified.

Field to sort notifications by. Valid values: 'created_at' (notification creation time, newest first), 'read_at' (when notification was read, most recent reads first), 'updated_at' (last modification time, newest first). Defaults to 'created_at' if not specified.

sort_by.description: Field to sort notifications by. Valid values: 'created_at' (notification creation time, newest first), 'read_at' (when notification was read, most recent reads first), 'updated_at' (last modification time, newest first). Defaults to 'created_at' if not specified.

IDiscussionBoardNotification.IRequest.description:
Search criteria, filtering options, and pagination parameters for retrieving a filtered list of member notifications.

Supports advanced notification filtering including notification type filtering (comment_reply, mention, article_moderation, comment_moderation), read status filtering (read vs unread), and full-text search on title and message fields. Pagination parameters (page, limit) control result set size and offset for handling large notification lists.

Used by GET /member/notifications endpoint to retrieve the authenticated member's complete notification history with advanced filtering and sorting capabilities. This DTO enables members to query their notification inbox with sophisticated search workflows.

is_read.description: Whether the notification has been read by the user. Set to true to mark notification as read (populates read_at), set to false to mark as unread (clears read_at). Used by users to track which notifications they have reviewed.

deleted_at.description: ISO 8601 UTC timestamp to soft-delete the notification from user's inbox. Set to current timestamp to delete notification (hide from user), set to null to restore/undelete a previously deleted notification. Supports soft deletion allowing recovery.

IDiscussionBoardNotification.IUpdate.description:
Update DTO for modifying notification state. Allows authenticated members to mark notifications as read/unread or soft-delete notifications from their inbox.

Supported operations:
- Mark as read: Set is_read to true to mark notification as read, which populates read_at with current timestamp
- Mark as unread: Set is_read to false to mark notification as unread, which clears read_at
- Delete (soft): Set deleted_at to current timestamp to hide notification from inbox
- Restore (undelete): Set deleted_at to null if notification was previously deleted

Ownership verification is enforced at the operation level - authenticated users can only update notifications belonging to their own account (where recipient_member_id matches their user ID).

notification_ids.description: Array of notification IDs to mark as read. Each ID must be a valid UUID format. All notifications must belong to the authenticated member - if any notification ID does not correspond to the member's own notification, the entire operation is rejected with authorization error.

IDiscussionBoardNotifications.IReadBulkR.description:
Request DTO for bulk marking multiple notifications as read. Accepts a list of notification IDs belonging to the authenticated member.

The operation validates that all provided notification IDs belong to the authenticated member before executing any updates. If any notification ID does not correspond to a notification owned by the authenticated user, the entire request is rejected with a 403 Forbidden or 400 Bad Request response, and no notifications are marked as read. This ensures atomicity and prevents members from marking other users' notifications as read.

This bulk operation improves efficiency when users want to clear their unread notification count, such as when visiting their notification inbox.

updated_count.description: The number of notifications that were successfully marked as read in this bulk operation. This count reflects actual database updates where the is_read flag was changed from false to true and the read_at timestamp was populated with the current server time in ISO 8601 UTC format. If all specified notifications were already marked as read, this value will be zero, but the operation still returns successfully. This value is always non-negative and represents the actual number of rows modified in the discussion_board_notifications table.

IDiscussionBoardNotifications.IReadBulkR.description:
Response confirming successful bulk marking of notifications as read. Contains the count of notifications that were actually updated to read status. This response indicates completion of the bulk read operation and provides feedback on how many notifications were affected by the update.

The response is returned after the system validates that all provided notification IDs belong to the authenticated member and successfully updates their is_read flags to true and populates the read_at timestamps with the current server time in UTC.

If no notifications were updated (for example, if all provided notifications were already marked as read or none matched the specified criteria), the system still returns a successful response with a count of zero, indicating that the operation completed without errors but affected no records.

unread_count.description: The total number of unread notifications currently available for the authenticated member. This is calculated by querying the discussion_board_notifications table and counting records where: recipient_member_id equals the authenticated member's ID, is_read is false (notification has not been marked as read), and deleted_at is null (notification has not been deleted by the user). The value will be zero if the member has no unread notifications. This value is always non-negative and represents the actual count of unread notification records in the system.

IDiscussionBoardNotificationCount.description:
Response containing the count of unread notifications for the authenticated member. This lightweight response provides a single numeric value representing how many notifications are currently unread for the authenticated user.

The count reflects notifications in the discussion_board_notifications table where the recipient_member_id matches the authenticated user's ID, the is_read flag is false (notification has not been viewed), and the deleted_at timestamp is null (notification has not been soft-deleted by the user).

This endpoint is typically used in user interface headers, navigation bars, or dashboards to display a notification badge indicating the number of unread notifications awaiting the user's attention. The count is recalculated in real-time with each request to ensure accuracy as notifications are created, read, or deleted.

id.description: Unique identifier for the member account in UUID format. System-generated at account creation and immutable thereafter. Used throughout the platform as the primary reference for this member.

email.description: Member's email address used for authentication and account management. Must be unique across all member accounts in the system. Used for login credentials, password recovery, and communication. This field is required and immutable after account creation for data integrity.

created_at.description: Timestamp when the member account was created in ISO 8601 UTC format. System-generated at registration and immutable thereafter. Represents the account's creation date used for audit trails and account age tracking.

updated_at.description: Timestamp when the member account was last modified in ISO 8601 UTC format. Updated whenever account details change such as email updates, password resets, or profile modifications. Tracks the most recent account modification for audit purposes.

oneOf.description: Account is in normal operating state with full access to platform features. Newly created accounts start in active status.
Account is temporarily suspended, typically for 7 days, due to community guideline violations. Suspended accounts cannot authenticate or create content.
Account is permanently banned due to severe or repeated violations. Banned accounts cannot authenticate or access any platform features.

account_status.description: Current status of the member account controlling access permissions. The account status determines whether the member can authenticate and create content on the platform.

deleted_at.description: Timestamp when the member account was soft-deleted or deactivated in ISO 8601 UTC format. NULL for active accounts. Set when member deletes their account or is deleted by administrators. Enables account recovery and maintains audit trail of deletions for compliance purposes.

IDiscussionBoardMember.description:
Complete profile information and account details for a registered member of the discussion board platform. Members are authenticated users who can create articles, post comments, and participate in discussions. This represents the core member entity with all account-level information needed for profile management, authentication, and authorization checks throughout the platform.

The member profile includes account metadata such as email address used for login and recovery, account status indicating whether the member can access the platform (active, suspended, or banned), and timestamp tracking for audit trails. The profile information is returned when members view their own account settings or when the system needs to reference member account details.

Members are distinct from moderators who have elevated administrative permissions. Each member maintains a unique email address for authentication and account recovery. The account_status field controls platform access and is managed by the moderation system when violations occur.

email.description: New email address for the member account. Must be a valid email format and unique across all member accounts in the system. This field is optional for updates - if not provided, the email remains unchanged. If provided, the system validates uniqueness to prevent duplicate email conflicts that would violate the unique constraint.

IDiscussionBoardMember.IUpdate.description:
Update request body for modifying an authenticated member's profile information. This schema defines which fields can be updated after account creation. Members can update their email address through this endpoint, subject to validation rules ensuring email uniqueness and format compliance.

All fields in this update schema are optional - members can choose to update only the fields they wish to modify. The system will preserve any fields not included in the update request. When the update is applied, the discussion_board_members record is modified with the new values and the updated_at timestamp is set to the current time.

Immutable fields such as id, created_at, and account_status cannot be modified through this endpoint. Account status changes are managed exclusively through the moderation system when violations or administrative actions occur.

id.description: Unique identifier for the article revision record. System-generated UUID that uniquely identifies this specific version of the article in the revision history.

discussion_board_article_id.description: Reference to the article this revision belongs to. Foreign key to discussion_board_articles.id. Links this revision record to the parent article being tracked.

editor_member_id.description: Reference to the member who made this edit if the editor was a regular member author. Null if this revision was made by a moderator. Foreign key to discussion_board_members.id. Populated only for member edits.

editor_moderator_id.description: Reference to the moderator who made this edit if the editor was a moderator. Null if this revision was made by a member author. Foreign key to discussion_board_moderators.id. Populated only for moderator edits.

title.description: Article title at the time this revision was created. Preserves the complete title history showing how the title evolved through edits. Between 3 and 200 characters as per article validation rules.

content.description: Article body content at the time this revision was created. Preserves the full historical content text immutably. Between 10 and 50,000 characters as per article validation rules. Critical for audit trail and potential rollback functionality.

edit_type.description: Type of edit that created this revision. Valid values: 'member_edit' (author editing their own article), 'moderator_edit' (moderator modifying article), 'system_update' (automated system change). Discriminator indicating who made the change and why.

change_reason.description: Optional reason or explanation for the edit, particularly important for moderator edits. Helps explain why content was modified and provides transparency to the article author. Can include notes about policy violations or corrections made.

created_at.description: Timestamp when this revision was created (when the edit was made). Stored in ISO 8601 UTC format. Used to track the sequence of edits chronologically and determine edit history ordering.

IDiscussionBoardArticleRevision.description:
Historical revision record for an article capturing a specific version from edit history.

Each article edit creates a new revision record preserving the complete state at that point in time. This snapshot-based approach enables full audit trails, change tracking, and potential rollback to previous versions. Revisions preserve both the content (title and body) and metadata about who made the change and why.

The record tracks whether edits were made by the article author (member) or by moderators, supporting different audit and transparency requirements for each type of modification. System edits are tracked separately for compliance purposes.

Revisions are immutable once created, forming a permanent historical record of all changes to the article.

id.description: Unique identifier for this article. System-generated UUID primary key. Used for referencing the article in moderation actions, revisions, and notifications.

title.description: Article title between 3 and 200 characters. Displayed in article listings and detail views. Quick identification of article topic for moderation assessment.

content.description: Main article body text between 10 and 50,000 characters. Contains the substantive discussion content that moderators must review for policy violations, misinformation, or inappropriate material.

status.description: Current article publication status. Valid values: 'published' (visible to all users), 'archived' (hidden from public view by moderators). Used to determine if article is currently accessible to community.

authorId.description: Unique identifier of the member who created this article. References discussion_board_members.id. Identifies article author for enforcement and communication purposes.

authorEmail.description: Email address of the article author. Denormalized for efficient display. Used for moderator communication about content violations or removal.

categoryId.description: Unique identifier of the category this article is classified under. References discussion_board_categories.id. Indicates whether article is economics or politics focused.

categoryName.description: Human-readable category name. Valid values: 'Economics' or 'Politics'. Indicates article's content classification.

viewCount.description: Number of times this article has been viewed. Used to assess article visibility and engagement. Higher view counts may indicate higher priority for moderation if problematic.

commentCount.description: Number of comments posted on this article. Indicates discussion activity and potential for heated exchanges or policy violations in comments.

createdAt.description: Timestamp when article was initially published. Stored in ISO 8601 UTC format. Used to assess how long problematic content has been visible.

updatedAt.description: Timestamp of most recent modification to article. Stored in ISO 8601 UTC format. Indicates whether article has been edited since creation.

flagCount.description: Number of times this article has been reported by users as violating community guidelines. Used as priority indicator for moderation review - higher counts suggest stronger need for review.

revision_number.description: Count of how many times the article has been edited. Starts at 0 when article is created. Incremented each time the article content or metadata is modified by the author or moderators. Used for audit trail and edit history tracking.

deleted_at.description: Soft delete timestamp. Set when article is deleted by author or moderator. NULL for active articles. Allows recovery and audit trail.

IDiscussionBoardArticle.IModerationView.description: Article presentation for moderation review. Includes all article details necessary for moderator assessment of policy compliance. Provides complete context including author, category, engagement metrics, user reports, and edit history for informed moderation decisions. Designed for moderation dashboard display and action determination.

id.description: Unique identifier for this comment. System-generated UUID primary key. Used for referencing comment in moderation actions and notifications.

content.description: Comment text between 1 and 5,000 characters. Contains user's discussion contribution that must be reviewed for policy violations including harassment, misinformation, or inappropriate language.

status.description: Current comment status indicating visibility state. Valid values: 'published' (visible to all users), 'moderated' (hidden with 'removed by moderator' message shown), 'deleted' (author-deleted). Used to determine if comment is currently visible.

authorId.description: Unique identifier of the member who posted this comment. References discussion_board_members.id. Identifies comment author for pattern analysis and enforcement.

authorEmail.description: Email address of the comment author. Denormalized for efficient display. Used for moderator communication about comment violations.

articleId.description: Unique identifier of the article this comment was posted on. References discussion_board_articles.id. Provides context about the article being discussed.

articleTitle.description: Title of the article this comment is on. Provides article context for understanding discussion topic.

parentCommentId.description: Unique identifier of the parent comment if this is a reply. References discussion_board_comments.id. Null for top-level comments. Used to show conversation context and reply chain.

threadDepth.description: Nesting level in the discussion thread. 0 for top-level comments, 1+ for replies. Indicates how deeply nested this comment is in the conversation.

replyCount.description: Number of replies to this comment. Indicates discussion activity on this comment and potential for concentrated policy violations.
